title: Quarterly Health Ops: Metric Stewardship & Renewal KPI Templates
summary: Working draft: compact, customer-facing KPI templates and steward guidance for QBRs focused on the four operational signals most tied to renewals — request latency, uptime/SLA, cost-per-token (or per-embedding), and cache hit rate. Intended for CS owners prepping renewal decks and for SRE/infra to validate the signals and instrumentation prior to QBRs.
metric_overview: Latency (p50, p95, p99) — definition: end-to-end request time from client HTTP POST to final token emission end. For streaming flows, use final message complete time. Exclude client-side retries; include backend queueing and model generation. Derivation formula: observed_time_ms = response_end_ts - request_received_ts; bucket by route/model/region. Notes: report medians and tail percentiles, plus % requests > threshold (e.g., >500ms for chat, >2s for long generation).

Uptime / Availability — definition: percentage of successful request attempts over total attempts, measured at the route level and translated to customer-visible SLA windows (30d). Successful = HTTP 200-series and non-empty generation. Exclude scheduled maintenance windows documented in advance. Use alerting SLOs (e.g., 99.95% monthly) and map incidents affecting renewals. For partial degradations (high latency but success), report separately as Performance Incidents.

Cost-per-token (or per-embedding) — definition: operational cost allocated to inference divided by billable units. For tokenized models: cost/token = infra_cost_tokens / billable_tokens_generated. For embedding customers: cost/vector = infra_cost_embeddings / vectors_processed. Include a companion metric: effective unit-revenue (customer billed rate minus cost/unit). Guidance: normalize to customer SKU/route so engineering and CS speak same units.

Cache Hit Rate — definition: fraction of requests where cached prefix/KV or response cache avoided full model execution. Calculation: cache_hits / cache_eligible_requests. Important to annotate eligibility rules (only exact-prefix, session pinned, or per-route). Provide breakdown: prefix cache vs response cache vs KV cache. Show effective cost reduction estimate from cache (estimated tokens avoided * avg cost/token).

measurement_notes: Instrumentation best practices: always tag events with customer_id, route_id, model_version, region, and deployment_tier (hosted/dedicated/private). For sampling, keep 100% of error traces, 10% of successful traces (biased to tail), and full-resolution logs for any request > configured SLO thresholds. Use consistent clock (monotonic server time) and record both service-received and service-complete timestamps to separate queueing vs compute time.
escalation_thresholds: Latency: if p95 increases >20% quarter-over-quarter OR p99 breaches SLO for >4 hours -> open incident and assign to runtime triage
Uptime: any customer-facing SLA drop below committed tier -> immediate engagement with account exec + escalation to oncall SRE
Cost: if cost/unit moves >15% and projected to increase gross margin below threshold -> cost review + consider model quantization/alternate routing
Cache: drop in cache hit-rate >10pp month-over-month for cache-eligible routes -> product investigation and possible change to cache TTL or prefixing strategy
playbook_runbook: Before QBR (T-14 days): assemble 30/90-day rolling metrics for the account; validate instrumentation (sample traces) and reconcile billing vs infra cost reports.

Before QBR (T-7 days): synthesize customer-impact narrative: wins (latency reductions, cost saves, cache improvements), risks (incidents, emergent patterns), and recommended asks (capacity, feature toggles).

QBR slide checklist: single KPI slide, incident timeline (if any), cost economics slide (unit cost vs billing), improvement roadmap (next 90 days), and explicit renewal asks (discount, dedicated capacity, support).
After QBR (T+3 days): publish action items with owners and SLAs into jira and follow-up in weekly renewal sync. Track progress in renewal tracker sheet (link in linked_artifacts).
open_questions: Should we switch cost reporting to per-invocation instead of per-token for large-context generation customers? Pros/cons listed in separate Confluence note (linked).
What default cache eligibility rule should CS present to customers (exact prefix only vs fuzzy-prefix)? Need product decision before next release window.
Do we want a small, standardized 1-page metric appendix for all QBR decks to reduce question time? (proposed template attached to this doc)
